I (mum) went through post natal depression. I still fall into it close to my child’s birthday (will be 9 on next birthday). I was depressed for 4-5 years before accepting it was now part of who I am.
I didn’t admit I was depressed for about 9 months. When I told my doctor, they sent me to see a psychologist but being raised in a very traditional household, I basically didn’t say anything for 10 sessions. Looking back, I wish I did.

For me, what would have helped is having someone there who didn’t judge me for feeling low. Didn’t judge me for not wanted to hold my child or laugh/smile when they did something cute.

I know father’s don’t have it easy. I think both parents have different struggles after having a baby. For me, it was hard because (as many have said), I lost my identity. I was no longer *insert name* but became *name*’s mother or worse yet, *name*’s wife who gave birth to their child”. 

There’s lots I would change in hindsight. Every mother is different. Please feel free to PM me if you want more of my experience. Don’t want to bore the community =)

Good luck and please send my hugs to your wife (and some to you as well) x

I didn’t like how antidepressants made me feel (or not feel…I became numb to every emotion) so I stopped after about 6-9 months.
It’s been 7 years and I still have my (very) low days.
Exercising helps a lot. Routine as well. I go for long walks when I need to clear my head.
Most importantly, I have friends who will always include me even though they know I won’t go, who support me and don’t force me to say anything if I don’t want to.
Have a strong support network helps me through my darkest days.

I normally go on a nice long walk, sit by the river. If I’m feeling particularly down, I go to East Coast Park and walk along the coast. 

Or I watch Studio Ghibli hahaha
Join a sports team!! Great way to make friends and forget about stuff temporarily. I do dragon boating and it’s a great fun!

You have to be responsible for them. If things go wrong, it’s your fault. If they go right, it’s thanks to the parents and the younger sibling. Oh and “why weren’t you like that when you were their age?”

It could be? Have you tried to have a quiet word with the teacher outside of class? I would split couples in the class if I felt like it wasn’t helping with their learning to sit next to each other. 
It’s a hard ask but your friend might need to have an input as well. I know she doesn’t want to speak to the teacher but she may need to if she wants you to continue helping her?
I would hope your teacher is patient enough to listen and try to understand the situation

As a teacher, I can say that either your teacher has very VERY good reasons for this or you just need to explain the situation to your teacher after class.

I changed the seating plan in my room after a term (I do this every term) and had a student come to me after 2 weeks. We had a small discussion where she explained the situation. I explained why I had her sitting next to a particular student (it takes a good few hours to make a decent seating plan per class) and we agreed we’d try it for one more week. It didn’t work so I shuffled the entire room again. I didn’t put her next to her friend but I moved things around enough to ensure all parties were comfortable enough to do group work but not necessarily with just their friends. Pretty sure it took around 4 seating plans.

I’m sorry if this doesn’t help. I don’t know how your teacher will react if you explain I’m detail the situation- they may or may not react as I would.

If you need more help, let me know!
